original_question: Is it true that one can always connect n points in a rectangle of side lengths √3 and (n − 1) by a set of length at most √3(n − 1) + o(1)?
target_in_paper: Section 2.5, Question 2.11: the rectangle upper-bound question for Steiner trees that arises from the asymptotic-extremal discussion on large numbers of terminals.
correct_elements: Your draft is aimed at the right problem family and, more specifically, matches the paper's rectangle question in the Steiner-tree asymptotics discussion. It correctly identifies the special rectangle with side lengths √3 and n−1, the fact that the input consists of n points, and the goal of bounding the total length needed to connect them.
missing_details: The exact target is Question 2.11 in Section 2.5, not Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3.
The paper asks for an exact upper bound of √3(n−1), not an asymptotic bound of √3(n−1)+o(1).
The quantifiers should be explicit: for every integer n and every configuration of n points contained in such a rectangle.
The ambient space is the Euclidean plane R^2.
In the paper, 'connect' means by a connected set; length is one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1.
To make the question stand alone, one should say that the set of points is contained in a rectangle of side lengths √3 and n−1 (equivalently, any congruent copy of such a rectangle).

The question belongs to the asymptotic-extremal Steiner-tree discussion: the preceding paragraph explains that this rectangle bound is proposed as a route to the conjecturally sharp reverse inequality for maximal Steiner-tree length.
The nearby context also records that the analogous problem for minimum spanning trees is open as well, but that is a neighboring remark rather than part of Question 2.11 itself.
There are no algebraic items here such as ring/field, homogeneity, degree bounds, or nilpotency assumptions; the relevant missing data are geometric definitions and quantifiers.
refined_question: For every integer n≥2, is it true that any set P⊂R^2 of n points contained in a rectangle of side lengths √3 and n−1 can be connected by a connected set Σ⊂R^2 with P⊂Σ and H^1(Σ)≤√3(n−1)?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the end of Section 2.5, where the paper formulates Question 2.11. The immediately preceding paragraph explains the asymptotic setting: one considers the maximal possible Steiner-tree length for n-point subsets of a planar compact set, notes a hexagonal-lattice lower bound, and then says that E. Paolini suggested proving a rectangle estimate in order to obtain the reverse inequality. Question 2.11 is then stated as the rectangle problem itself. To make the question stand alone, the Section 2 definition of a Steiner tree must be imported: one is minimizing one-dimensional Hausdorff measure among connected sets whose union with the terminal set is connected, so the natural self-contained phrasing is in terms of a connected set Σ with H^1(Σ) bounded above. Your draft is close on the geometry, but it weakens the paper's exact bound to an asymptotic '+o(1)' term and leaves the ambient space, quantifiers, and length notion implicit.
